messages.subject: Reults from scanmqm() were vastly different from scanone() and scantwo(). Are they valid/reliable?
messages.subject_clean: Reults from scanmqm() were vastly different from scanone() and scantwo(). Are they valid/reliable?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm trying to use multiple QTL mapping (scanmqm()) on a population of 178 recombinant inbred lines with 1221 markers. On average, my markers are about 1 cM apart.

I build an intial list of 153 cofactors from different autocofactors() runs as suggested by Danny Arends. (https://groups.google.com/forum/?utm_medium=email&utm_source=footer#!msg/rqtl-disc/Q1AJp7_6xDw/uloRef8nBQAJ) I specified that each pair of cofactors must be at least 5 cM apart, resulting in a list of 153 cofactors ready for scanmqm() to use (Fig. 1).

Fig.1 Genetic map with initial 153 cofactors for scanmqm() function marked as red dots.

Then I ran scanmqm() with that list and got LOD results that were vastly different from scanone(..., method = "ehk") results (Fig. 2).

Fig. 2 Comparison of LOD profiles from scanone() and scanmqm().

The MQM model that was returned from scanmqm consisted of 22 'QTLs' that, as I understand it, were used as covariate when testing for distant QTLs.

Fig. 3 is the LOD profile from plotLodProfile() after running refineqtl() on the model returned by mqmscan().

Fig. 3 One-dimensional LOD profiles for each QTL from MQM model. Dotted line is genome-wide significance at alpha = 0.01 level from mqmpermutation().

However, when I used scantwo() function (Fig. 4), I could not detect any evidence for epistatic interactions, not even for the three QTLs I identified from scanone().

Fig. 4 Results from scantwo() function.

My questions are:

Did I over fit the MQM model with 22 ramaining cofactor, given the population that I have (178 recombinant inbred lines, 175 of which were typed)?
For LOD profile around Q1 (overall MQM LOD profile, Fig. 2), did the MQM model used all Q2-Q22 as covariates and how did it do that given the population only consists of 175 typed RILs?
How can there be so many more QTLs detected by MQM method whilst only three were detected from both scanone() abd scantwo()? Are the MQM results reliable?
Are my mqmpermutation(..., cofactors = cof.mqm, scanfunction = mqmscan, method = "permutation", n.perm = 10000, n.cluster = 8) results a bit strange that there were only 10 unique maximum LOD scores and 10% of permutations were at the highest value of 3.639 whilst the highest LOD score from scanmqm() was 16.474. (LOD score distribution seen in Fig. 5)?

Fig. 5 Distribution of maximum LOD score from mqmpermutation().

messages.subject: Re: Reults from scanmqm() were vastly different from scanone() and scantwo(). Are they valid/reliable?
messages.subject_clean: Reults from scanmqm() were vastly different from scanone() and scantwo(). Are they valid/reliable?
messages.body_plain:
My answers are under your questions:

> My questions are:
>
> Did I over fit the MQM model with 22 ramaining cofactor, given the population that I have (178 recombinant inbred lines, 175 of which were typed)?

No in theory not. The MQM routine can handle upto (n individuals - 10) = ~ 165 cofactors, with 155 you're below this theorectical threshold,
However,I would not go that high. My advice is to take ~ 100 cofactors into the model selection phase to prevent overfitting

> For LOD profile around Q1 (overall MQM LOD profile, Fig. 2), did the MQM model used all Q2-Q22 as covariates and how did it do that given the population only consists of 175 typed RILs?

Yes, this is exactly what the MQM routine does. MQM compensates for all other cofactors, in your case you loose 21 out of
174 degrees of freedom in the statistical test, this is perfectly reasonable

> How can there be so many more QTLs detected by MQM method whilst only three were detected from both scanone() abd scantwo()? Are the MQM results reliable?

scanone does not compensate for the cofactors used in the model, this is why MQM has higher statistical power to detect effects.
However you should adjust the threshold using permutations where you include the same number of initial cofactors, my guess is
that your scanone defined threshold is too low for the MQM routine.

> Are my mqmpermutation(..., cofactors = cof.mqm, scanfunction = mqmscan, method = "permutation", n.perm = 10000, n.cluster = 8) results a bit strange that there were only 10 unique maximum LOD scores and 10% of permutations were at the highest value of 3.639 whilst the highest LOD score from scanmqm() was 16.474. (LOD score distribution seen in Fig. 5)?

this is really worrisome, I think something goes wrong in the permutation routine (too many initial cofactors), or the phenotype that you're mapping is not a normal distribution

If you want me too look into this please send me a copy of your data set (will be handled confidentially) per email: Danny....@gmail.com

Kind regards,
Danny

messages.subject: c.cross problem, possibly bug?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Karl,

I'm experiencing an error when trying to merge a F2 cross object and a BC cross object. They have exactly the same chromosomes, markers, etc. I think it's a bug and I've detailed it below but I wanted to check that I'm not doing something wrong.

I also have a few questions:
1) given that my F2 and BC crosses are genotyped at exactly the same locations, I could just concatenate my genotype and phenotype files before reading them into R/qtl. How would that affect my results compared to using c.cross?
2) Also, with the output from c.cross, do I need to add one of the new phenotype columns (cross1, cross2, cross, for example) as a covariate or is the batch/cross type covariate automatically inputted somehow?

Thank you,
Andrew

The error message reads:

Error in dimnames(geno[[j]]$prob) <- dimnames(x$geno[[j]]$prob) :
  length of 'dimnames' [1] not equal to array extent

I believe this is caused by a bug in util.R at line 1788, when R/qtl is trying to name the concatenated genotype array. I believe you could fix it by replacing line 1788 with the following:
dimnames(geno[[j]]$prob)[[1]] <- character(length = sum(n.ind))
dimnames(geno[[j]]$prob)[[2]] <- dimnames(args[[wh]]$geno[[j]]$prob)[[2]]
dimnames(geno[[j]]$prob)[[3]] <- dimnames(args[[wh]]$geno[[j]]$prob)[[3]]
And then add on (what was previously) line 1793:
dimnames(geno[[j]]$prob)[[1]][wh] = dimnames(args[[i]]$geno[[j]]$prob)[[1]]

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] c.cross problem, possibly bug?
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for your response. This is a bit embarrassing... Upon trying to create a small example file to play with, I am unable to recapitulate my error. I am using MSG, so I used read.cross.msg to read in the genotype probabilities and I'm guessing this may be causing the merging problem.

When I first tried this, I read in the BC1 and F2 data separately, then merged them. However, this resulted in my BC1 genotypes being switched to heterozygous. I think this is because read.cross.msg somehow read in the BC1 genotypes "backwards" and R/qtl thought I had invalid genotypes for a backcross. (I though had fixed this problem, but I guess not completely)

I'm wondering if it's possible to entirely circumvent this problem. Since I ran MSG on the BC1 and F2 individuals all together, all the individuals' genotypes are in a single file with the same markers and everything. Is there a difference between reading the BC1 and F2 in separately and then merging them, as opposed to reading in the combined genotype probabilities and then setting cross$pheno$crosstype?

Thank you,
Andrew

messages.subject: Question about % variance explained
messages.body_plain:
Dear Karl,

I apologize that this question is pretty similar to some other questions. When estimating the effects of the QTL with fitqtl, I get a % variance explained by the model and % variance of each QTL (the drop one analysis). The % variance explained by the model is always higher (sometimes quite substantially) than the % variances of the individual QTL/covariates.

I see a few people saying that the % variance of the model is lower than the sum of the individual variances due to correlated genotypes/covariates. But I'm not sure why the model would be able to explain more variance than the individual components. Do you have any insight about why this is?

Thank you very much,
Andrew

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Question about % variance explained
messages.body_plain:
The overall percent variance explained will only equal the sum of the individual QTLs' percent variance explained if the genotypes at the QTLs are perfectly independent. Whether the overall percent variance explained is > or < the sum of the individual QTLs' PVE depends on the positive or negative association between QTL genotypes.

karl

I am working with an F2 population to make a genetic map following your manual and ASMap, but I get huge LGs (my map is covering around 5000 cM), and it looks weird.

I tried to check if I have a genotyping error following the manual, using the cross-file used to build the last genetic map (I have attached a pdf with the results). Do you think it could be better to perform the genotyping error analysis with the first cross (with raw data), before deleting these genotypes with errors?. Or do you think I can´t build a genetic map with this data?

I would appreciate your help,

Best,

Alicia

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] genotyping errors
messages.body_plain:
I don't think I can provide any useful advice with the information provided.

I would spend too much time looking for individual genotyping errors or trying to estimate the genotyping error rate. Both are difficult or impossible in advance of having a confident genetic map.

I would focus mainly on omitting bad samples and setting aside badly behaved markers. A key question is whether the linkage groups are huge because of a few large intervals or if there's an overall map expansion.

karl

messages.subject: Effect of each QTL after refine.qtl
messages.subject_clean: Effect of each QTL after refine.qtl
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have followed the refine.qtl step to improve marker positions and LOD score and did fitqtl with my refine.qtl, which I got a summary of the sum of LOD score and %var explained. I'm wondering how to get the LOD score and %var explained for each of my potential QTL?

The code and results I used for these two steps are:
>
> >refine.qtl <- refineqtl(ourdata, qtl=multiqtl, covar = parent)
> > summary(fitqtl(ourdata, qtl=refine.qtl, covar = parent, method = "hk", dropone = F))
>
> fitqtl summary
>
> Method: multiple imputation
> Model:  normal phenotype
> Number of observations : 354
>
> Full model result
> ----------------------------------
> Model formula: y ~ Q1 + Q2 + Q3 + Q4 + Q5 + Q6 + Q7 + V1
>
>        df        SS        MS     LOD     %var Pvalue(Chi2) Pvalue(F)
> Model  15  56.44003 3.7626686 42.3925 42.39047            0         0
> Error 338  76.70317 0.2269325
> Total 353 133.14320

And I'm hoping to get a breakdown of LOD and %var of Q1 to Q7 and V1.

Thank you very much!

messages.subject: Overlaying CIM plots
messages.body_plain:
Karl,

Instead of plotting three composite intervals into 3 separate panels, I would like to overlay them.

The three CIMs are with windows of 20, 40, and Inf. I am able to plot any combination of 2 of these (in addition to the original scanone) with (for example):

plot(qtl.scan1, cim.20, cim.inf, chr = chr)

giving me:

However, when I try plotting all three:

plot(qtl.scan1, cim.20, cim.40, cim.inf, chr = chr)

I get the following error:

Error in `+.scanone`(lodcolumn, 2) : Input should have class "scanone".

Is there any way to fix this?

Thanks,

Nathaniel

messages.subject: write.cross for 4way cross
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I used JoinMap files (.loc, .qua, and .map) as input files to r/qtl to QTL analysis for 4way cross.
I tried to save the resulted cross file using write.cross function, but it works only for intercross, backcross, RI, double haploid, and haploid data.
Can anyone suggest a way to save my  cross file.
This is the code I used.

# inputing the data generated from JoinMap

x= read.cross("mapqtl", genfile="Genotypes.loc", phefile="Phenotypes.qua", mapfile="Map.map")

#save x

#write.cross(x,format = "csv",filestem = "Ris_Cabmap")

Thank you,
Dilmini
